name: Ascending arousal system and the sleep-wake flip-flop switch
function: Maintenance of cortical arousal and wakefulness, and the reciprocal switching between wake- and sleep-promoting circuits

steps.cellBodies: Pedunculopontine (PPT) and laterodorsal tegmental (LDT) cholinergic nuclei (midbrain/pons)
courseVia: ascending cholinergic projection of the reticular activating system

evidence.quote: The lateral and dorsal pedunculopontine tegmentum contains primarily cholinergic neurons in neighboring groups within the midbrain and pons.
Cholinergic neurons project to the thalamus and cortex, promoting desynchronization of the brain,
Two cell masses, the laterodorsal tegmental (LDT) and pedunculopontine tegmental (PPT) nuclei, both situated in the tegmentum of the caudal midbrain and rostral pons.
These nuclei contain numerous neurons that use acetylcholine as a neurotransmitter.
The dorsal branch, which includes numerous cholinergic fibres from the LDT and PPT, passes to the thalamus itself and the reticular thalamic nucleus

Fibres ascending from the mesopontine cholinergic (LDT, PPT), noradrenergic (LC), and serotoninergic (DR, CS) cell groups and from other parts of the reticular formation together form an ascending arousal system (AAS).
Cholinergic neurons that project to the forebrain are found in the pedunculopontine and laterodorsal tegmental nuclei (PPT and LDT).
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

evidence.quote: PPT/LDT cholinergic neurons innervate many subcortical regions that influence arousal, but unlike the BF cholinergic neurons, their innervation of the cortex is sparse.
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

steps.terminatesIn: cortex, thalamus, hypothalamus and basal forebrain

evidence.quote: The locus coeruleus is located within the upper dorsolateral pons of the brainstem. It is activated directly by orexin from the lateral hypothalamus, and in response, releases norepinephrine.
Noradrenergic neurons clustered in the locus coeruleus (LC), in the rostral pontine tegmentum
The monoaminergic cell groups at the mesopontine level which project to the forebrain include the noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC) and the serotoninergic dorsal and median raphe nuclei
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

evidence.quote: The raphe nuclei are located midline throughout the brainstem within the pons, midbrain, and medulla. The majority of neurons located in the raphe nuclei are serotonergic.
Mesencephalic serotoninergic neurons in the dorsal raphe (DR) and central superior (CS) nuclei.
The ventral branch of the ascending arousal system, which consists mainly of serotoninergic and noradrenergic fibres, enters the hypothalamus.
The monoaminergic cell groups at the mesopontine level which project to the forebrain include the noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC) and the serotoninergic dorsal and median raphe nuclei
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

evidence.quote: VLPO-related inhibitory output targets multiple wake-promoting nuclei—including the histaminergic tuberomammillary nucleus (TMN), noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC), serotonergic raphe nuclei, and cholinergic neurons of the basal forebrain—thereby lowering cortical arousal and stabilizing sleep states
evidence.species: human (review synthesising rodent and human data)

evidence.quote: A group of histaminergic cells clustered in the tuberomamillary nucleus (TMN) in the posterior hypothalamus
The TMN neurons contain several other neurotransmitters and modulators in addition to histamine, including GABA, galanin, and substance P
Histaminergic neurons in the tuberomammillary nucleus (TMN) have similar projection targets and firing patterns
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

evidence.quote: Axons from these cell groups predominantly target the lateral hypothalamus, basal forebrain and cerebral cortex, where they terminate extensively, particularly in the prefrontal cortex.
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

steps.cellBodies: Orexin/hypocretin neurons of the lateral hypothalamus
steps.terminatesIn: locus coeruleus, tuberomammillary nucleus, raphe nuclei, basal forebrain and cortex

evidence.quote: these centers are activated by the lateral hypothalamus (LH), which releases the neuropeptide orexin in response to the light hitting the eyes, which then stimulates arousal and the transition from sleep to waking.
A group of diffusely arranged neurons in the intermediate region of the hypothalamus characterized by presence of the neuropeptide orexin (also known as hypocretin)

noradrenergic and serotoninergic fibres of the ventral branch of the ascending arousal system are joined by histaminergic fibres from the TMN, orexinergic fibres from the PFG, and further rostrally by numerous axons from the cholinergic BT
There is evidence that degeneration or agenesis of the orexinergic hypothalamic neurons in humans
the lateral hypothalamus contains neurons producing the orexin neuropeptides (orexin-A and –B, also known as hypocretin-1 and 2)
They send axons to the entire cerebral cortex, as well as to the brainstem and basal forebrain, with particularly intense input to the TMN and the LC

steps.cellBodies: Ventrolateral preoptic nucleus (VLPO), GABA/galanin co-expressing and non-galanin GABAergic neurons
steps.terminatesIn: tuberomammillary nucleus, locus coeruleus, raphe nuclei, basal forebrain and vlPAG/LDT-PPT (reciprocal inhibition of arousal nuclei)

evidence.quote: sleep–wake control has classically been conceptualized through the “flip-flop switch” model, in which sleep-promoting preoptic neurons and arousal-promoting systems engage in reciprocal inhibition to permit rapid and stable state transitions
evidence.species: human (review synthesising rodent and human data)

evidence.quote: including GABA/galanin co-expressing neurons, non-galanin GABAergic neurons, and glutamatergic neurons—contribute differentially to non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, rapid eye movement (REM)-associated processes
The VLPO sends descending projections to the various components of the ascending arousal system
evidence.species: rat (VLPO characterised in this passage from Sherin et al.'s rat studies)

evidence.quote: Because the VLPO neurons synthesize GABA and galanin, their descending projections are likely to be inhibitory.
evidence.species: rat (VLPO characterised in this passage from Sherin et al.'s rat studies)

evidence.quote: Thus a reciprocal inhibitory interaction likely exists between the sleep-promoting VLPO and the monoaminergic wake-promoting centres in the caudal hypothalamus and brain stem.
evidence.species: human (general synthesis, based partly on rodent tracing data)

evidence.quote: When VLPO neurons fire rapidly during sleep, they would inhibit the monoaminergic cell groups, thus disinhibiting and reinforcing their own firing.
evidence.species: cross-species (Saper et al. model, quoted verbatim by Nieuwenhuys)

evidence.quote: Similarly, when monoamine neurons fire at a high rate during wakefulness, they would inhibit the VLPO, thereby disinhibiting their own firing
evidence.species: cross-species (Saper et al. model, quoted verbatim by Nieuwenhuys)

evidence.quote: VLPO neurons, containing the inhibitory neurotransmitters GABA and galanin, innervate other components of the ascending arousal system as well, including the LC, raphe system, periaqueductal gray matter, parabrachial nucleus, and lateral hypothalamic area
We propose that this mutually antagonistic relationship can give rise to behavior similar to that seen with a flip-flop switch
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

evidence.quote: VLPO and MnPO sleep-active neurons are GABAergic, and VLPO neurons also produce the neuropeptide galanin.
One model proposes that this mutual inhibition generates patterns of activity akin to an electrical flip-flop switch
evidence.species: cross-species synthesis (rodent-based model applied to human sleep-wake circuitry)

steps.cellBodies: Ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) GABAergic REM-off neurons
courseVia: projections to pontine LDT/PPT cholinergic REM-promoting circuitry
steps.terminatesIn: laterodorsal tegmental (LDT) and pedunculopontine tegmental (PPT) nuclei
steps.neurotransmitter: GABA (vlPAG output); dopaminergic neurons also present in vlPAG per brief

evidence.quote: inhibition of vlPAG GABAergic REM-off neurons disinhibits pontine REM-promoting circuitry, thereby facilitating REM expression
However, at onset of REM sleep, noradrenergic and serotoninergic neurons are inhibited by a local GABAergic element, which leads to disinhibition of the cholinergic neurons.
GABAergic neurons in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter and the adjacent lateral pontine tegmentum (vlPAG/LPT; shown in gold) fire during non-REM states to inhibit entry into REM sleep.
Injections of retrograde tracers into the SLD identified major GABAergic inputs from the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (vlPAG) and adjacent lateral pontine tegmentum (LPT)

lesions.site: Bilateral paramedian midbrain/pontine tegmentum and ascending reticular activating system
lesions.deficit: Coma: sustained unresponsiveness with eyes closed, unarousable to vigorous stimulation

evidence.quote: Acute impairments of consciousness include coma which is defined as a “state of unresponsiveness in which the patient lies with eyes closed and cannot be aroused to respond appropriately to stimuli even with vigorous stimulation”

conflicts.issue: Identity of the GABAergic nucleus responsible for suppressing the mesopontine cholinergic (LDT/PPT) REM-generating system outside of REM sleep

positions.claim: Original batch (Saper-review-derived) attributes tonic REM-off inhibition specifically to GABAergic neurons of the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter and adjacent lateral pontine tegmentum (vlPAG/LPT)
positions.quote: GABAergic neurons in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter and the adjacent lateral pontine tegmentum (vlPAG/LPT; shown in gold) fire during non-REM states to inhibit entry into REM sleep.

positions.claim: Nieuwenhuys instead attributes tonic REM-off suppression of LDT/PPT to the noradrenergic locus coeruleus and serotoninergic dorsal/central-superior raphe cells themselves, with REM onset triggered by an unspecified 'local GABAergic element' inhibiting those monoaminergic cells, rather than naming the vlPAG as the GABAergic REM-off nucleus
positions.quote: There is evidence that normally the noradrenergic LC and serotoninergic DR and CS are tonically active and inhibit the mesopontine cholinergic system.

conflicts.issue: Downstream target of vlPAG/LPT GABAergic REM-off neurons: LDT/PPT cholinergic nuclei versus the sublaterodorsal nucleus (SLD)

positions.claim: vlPAG/LPT GABAergic REM-off neurons inhibit REM sleep by projecting to the sublaterodorsal nucleus (SLD), which forms the mutually-inhibitory core REM switch with the vlPAG/LPT, rather than projecting directly to the LDT/PPT cholinergic cell groups named in the existing step
positions.quote: Injections of retrograde tracers into the SLD identified major GABAergic inputs from the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (vlPAG) and adjacent lateral pontine tegmentum (LPT)

unsourced.text: Dopaminergic neurons of the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) are described in current sleep literature as an additional wake-promoting monoaminergic group; the vlPAG dopamine cell group's projections to hypothalamus/basal forebrain specifically were not found described with a quotable, openable source in this session.

Dopaminergic neurons of the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) as an additional wake-promoting monoaminergic group, and their specific projections to hypothalamus/basal forebrain, were not found described in the opened Nieuwenhuys hypothalamus (ch10) or reticular-formation (ch22) chapters; the vlPAG's role as a discrete GABAergic REM-off nucleus, named as such, was likewise not found (see conflict above).

Dopaminergic neurons of the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) as an additional wake-promoting monoaminergic group, and their specific projections to hypothalamus/basal forebrain, were not found described with a quotable statement in S4 or S5 in this session.

The generic 'bilateral paramedian midbrain/pontine tegmentum' coma lesion claim from the original batch was not itself re-confirmed verbatim in S4/S5, although both sources support closely related coma-producing lesions of the basal forebrain and parabrachial nucleus (see new lesion entries above).
